banner.definition: Long strip of cloth or paper used for decoration or advertising.

bunting.definition: A loosely woven fabric used for flags, etc.

balloon.definition: A flexible bag filled with air or gas for decoration.

streamer.definition: A long narrow strip of paper or fabric used as decoration.

lantern.definition: A portable lamp used for light while camping.

garland.definition: Flower arrangement consisting of a circular band of foliage or flowers for ornamental purposes.

flag.definition: A piece of cloth attached to a pole as a symbol.

ribbon.definition: Any long object resembling a thin line.

confetti.definition: Small pieces or streamers of colored paper that are thrown around on festive occasions (as at a wedding).

pi-ata.definition: A decorated container, often made from paper, that is filled with small treats and used in a celebration game.
pi-ata.exampleUsage: The colorful piñata hung securely in the party area.

wreath.definition: Flower arrangement consisting of a circular band of foliage or flowers for ornamental purposes.

paper-flower.definition: A decorative flower made from folded, cut, or shaped paper.
paper-flower.exampleUsage: Paper flowers decorated the festival stage.

barbecue.definition: A cookout in which food is cooked over an open fire.

kebab.definition: Cubes of meat marinated and cooked on a skewer usually with vegetables.

pizza-slice.definition: One triangular or wedge-shaped portion cut from a pizza.
pizza-slice.exampleUsage: The food stand served one pizza slice on a paper plate.

taco.definition: (ethnic slur) offensive term for a person of Mexican descent.

samosa.definition: Small turnover of Indian origin filled with vegetables or meat and fried and served hot.

spring-roll.definition: A thin pancake is filled with minced meat and vegetables, rolled up, and fried.

waffle.definition: Pancake batter baked in a waffle iron.

fruit-skewer.definition: Pieces of fruit arranged on a small stick or skewer for serving.
fruit-skewer.exampleUsage: The fruit skewer included melon and grapes.

roasted-corn.definition: Corn cooked using dry heat until tender and lightly browned.
roasted-corn.exampleUsage: The food stall sold roasted corn.

doughnut.definition: A sweet fried cake, often shaped like a ring.

fried-chicken.definition: Chicken cooked by frying in hot oil or fat until the outside is browned and crisp.
fried-chicken.exampleUsage: The festival menu included fried chicken.

lemonade.definition: A cold sweet drink made with lemons, water, and sugar.

smoothie.definition: A thick smooth drink consisting of fresh fruit pureed with ice cream or yoghurt or milk.

hot-chocolate.definition: A warm, sweet beverage prepared by combining cocoa powder with milk and sugar.

milkshake.definition: Frothy drink of milk and flavoring and sometimes fruit or ice cream.

juice-box.definition: A small sealed carton containing a single serving of juice.
juice-box.exampleUsage: The family area provided a juice box with each meal.

cotton-candy.definition: A light, fluffy sweet made from spun sugar.

caramel-apple.definition: An apple coated in a sticky candy shell, usually made from caramelized sugar.

popcorn.definition: Small pieces of corn heated until they burst into white pieces.

churro.definition: A long fried pastry covered with sugar and cinnamon.

ice-cream.definition: A cold, frozen dessert usually made with milk or cream, sugar, and added flavorings.

stage.definition: A large platform on which people can stand and can be seen by an audience.

band.exampleUsage: The band was used during the activity.

singer.definition: United States inventor of an improved chain-stitch sewing machine (1811-1875).
singer.exampleUsage: The singer was used during the activity.

dj-booth.definition: A designated area where a disc jockey controls recorded music and audio equipment.
dj-booth.exampleUsage: The DJ booth was beside the main stage.

dance-floor.definition: An open area intended for people to dance on.
dance-floor.exampleUsage: Colorful lights shone over the dance floor.

fire-dancer.definition: A performer who uses burning props as part of a professional staged performance.
fire-dancer.exampleUsage: Trained professionals performed the fire-dancer act behind a safety barrier.

acrobat.definition: An athlete who performs acts requiring skill and agility and coordination.

stilt-walker.definition: A performer who walks on very tall stilts.

face-painter.definition: A person who paints designs on people’s faces.

parade.definition: A public procession with performers, music, and decorated vehicles.

carnival-game.definition: A simple game at a fair or festival, often played for entertainment or small prizes.
carnival-game.exampleUsage: The carnival game used soft rings and marked targets.

photo-booth.definition: A small enclosed space where people take photographs.

arts-and-crafts.definition: Creative activities that involve making useful or decorative objects by hand. They often use familiar techniques such as drawing, painting, sewing, carving, woodworking, or pottery.
arts-and-crafts.arabicTranslation: مصطلح مرتبط بالموضوع يُسمّى «ارتس اند كرافتس»

puppet-show.definition: A staged performance in which puppets portray the characters instead of human actors.

magic-show.definition: A performance in which an entertainer creates illusions or seemingly impossible effects.
magic-show.exampleUsage: Families gathered near the stage for the magic show.

talent-contest.definition: A competition in which participants perform skills such as music, dance, or comedy.
talent-contest.exampleUsage: Students entered the festival talent contest.

treasure-hunt.definition: A game in which players follow a sequence of clues to locate objects that have been hidden.

costume-contest.definition: A competition in which participants are judged on costumes they wear or create.
costume-contest.exampleUsage: The costume contest had categories for different age groups.

raffle.definition: A lottery in which the prizes are goods rather than money.

ticket.definition: A printed or electronic pass that allows entry to a ride or park.

wristband.definition: A band worn around the wrist to show admission or permission.

map.definition: A drawing that shows places, routes, and geographical features.

folding-chair.definition: A portable chair designed to collapse into a flat shape when it is put away.

sunscreen.definition: A cream spread on the skin.

water-bottle.definition: A container used for carrying drinking water.

rain-poncho.definition: A loose waterproof outer garment worn over clothing to keep rain off.
rain-poncho.exampleUsage: She kept a rain poncho in her festival bag.

portable-charger.definition: A small rechargeable battery device used to supply power to phones or other electronics away from an outlet.
portable-charger.exampleUsage: The portable charger restored power to the phone.

string-lights.definition: Small electric lights connected along a wire for decoration.

fireworks.definition: Bright coloured lights that explode in the night sky.

live-music.definition: Music performed by musicians in person rather than played only from a recording.
live-music.exampleUsage: The festival featured live music on the main stage.

dance.definition: Taking a series of rhythmical steps (and movements) in time to music.

magician.definition: A performer who uses tricks and illusions to entertain people.

face-paint.definition: Cosmetic paint designed to be applied to the face for decoration or performance.
face-paint.exampleUsage: The artist used washable face paint for a simple design.

clown.definition: A performer who wears a funny costume and tries to make people laugh.

corn-dog.definition: A sausage covered in batter and served on a stick.

funnel-cake.definition: A sweet cake made by pouring batter through a funnel and frying it.

pretzel.definition: A twisted baked snack covered with salt.

candy-apple.definition: An apple covered with a hard sweet coating.
